content: {"summary":"During the early‑morning window on 23 July 2026 both notification‑worker pods experienced slow DNS lookups and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors, traced to the cluster‑wide ndots:5 setting that caused many queries for short names, saturating the libuv worker pool and leading to lost replies and retries that added ~10 s latency.","likely_cause":"Cluster default ndots:5 caused excessive DNS queries for short names, saturating the 4‑thread libuv worker pool and resulting in timeouts and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Both notification-worker pods showed slow DNS lookups and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#0"],"quote":"Both workers resolved names slowly, and a few lookups finished in `EAI_AGAIN`, the status that means a try‑again."},{"text":"The cluster default ndots:5 caused short names to generate many DNS queries, leading to slow lookups.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#7","INC-0179#0"],"quote":"The name has fewer dots than the pod's `ndots`."},{"text":"Lost DNS replies and retries added about 10 seconds latency to some lookups.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#5"],"quote":"Two lost replies on two different queries of the same lookup, each recovered by its retry, cost about 10 s."}]}
